project_justification.gap: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR supplies WATE lower-bound templates in its estimator-bounded source class, whereas BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE supplies a lower-rate statement for one mean functional in a different uniformly overlapped structure-agnostic source class. Neither published class is nested with the present dyadic-shell public-function experiment, so neither citation supports class inclusion or a transferred minimax theorem. The accepted-bank runs \texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap\_polynomial\_upper\_match} and \texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_heterogeneity\_frontier\_v1} also study the full-population binary ATE, but under fixed two-sided overlap and finite discrete covariate occupancy. With \(d\) denoting the number of covariate cells, the former establishes the binary-outcome rare-cell MSE frontier \(n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]\); the latter gives a radius-indexed MSE bracket for real outcomes under bounded conditional means and approximate cell-effect homogeneity. Their obstructions are unknown discrete cell occupancy and cell-effect heterogeneity, whereas the present experiment has an infinite standard-Borel covariate support, dyadic propensity decay, deterministic public nuisance functions, and only global \(L^2(P_X)\) certificates. These law and information classes are non-nested, and neither accepted-bank result transfers a converse, rate, or honest-length theorem to the present class. Weak-overlap papers give trimming rules, irregular limits, or sufficient Wald conditions rather than this finite-sample four-risk frontier with an evaluable honest interval.

prose_updates.interpretation: The regular-benchmark reduction is only an algebraic check: as \(\kappa\to\infty\), the treated side has the same parametric-plus-product form as the verified published lower-bound templates after their explicit radius identifications. Bonvini's attested one-functional statement is used only for the treated-side mapping \(\varepsilon_n=r_{1n}\), \(\delta_n=r_{en}\); no control-arm term is attributed to that source. The shell class and the regular comparator class are disjoint, so the calculation establishes neither minimax equivalence nor inclusion transfer. The accepted-bank runs \texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap\_polynomial\_upper\_match} and \texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_heterogeneity\_frontier\_v1} study the same full-population binary ATE only within fixed-overlap finite-discrete-occupancy experiments. The first isolates unknown rare-cell occupancy for binary outcomes, and the second isolates approximate cell-effect heterogeneity for real outcomes with bounded conditional means. Those experiments and this infinite-support, dyadic weak-overlap, public-global-\(L^2(P_X)\) experiment are non-nested; no lower bound, rate, or honest-length conclusion is transferred between them. The accepted policy-regret and continuous-exposure clamp frontiers answer non-nested causal decision problems under non-nested law classes.
